messages:
marta: FYI customer reporting a sudden spike of 502/504s on hosted inference in us-west-2 starting ~13:02 UTC. Customer says streaming responses truncated and their SDK is entering a retry loop. They can reproduce consistently for a short window. Attaching repro and headers below.

ops-bot: alert: ingress-504-spike us-west-2 13:01:23 - 13:06:12; peak qps 180; affected route: /v1/generate (streaming) - svc:edge-router

juan: Can you paste a minimal curl and the request-id from the customer logs? Also which SDK version are they using and do they show Authorization header length / token rotation frequency?

marta: customer says SDK v0.9.1. They rotate short-lived tokens every 30s. Example curl they used:

```bash
curl -i -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-large","input":"short prompt","stream":true}' \\n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

They included Connection: keep-alive and a 3s client timeout. Request-id header from their logs: rwd-20260317-9a7bcd.

lex: I pulled edge-router traces for that request-id range. We're seeing a surge of new TLS handshakes and ephemeral connections around 13:01:50 -> 13:03:00. Upstream router queues briefly exceeded per-worker fd limits and returned 502/504 while backend pools were at capacity. Root cause looks like connection churn caused by token rotation + SDK creating new connections instead of reusing. Also saw socket close/reset from auth proxy during token swap.

emily: On the runtime side, model pool p95 tokenization+first-chunk time jumped from 400ms -> 1.8s during the spike (KV cache cold starts + slightly larger batch expansion). When edge returns 502 the SDK retries; because tokens rotate every 30s we see retry fanout and more new connections. The combination pushed router queueing over threshold.

juan: Repro steps for us: run a small harness that rotates tokens frequently and does many short streaming requests with connection: keep-alive disabled vs enabled to see diff. Example python snippet: 

```python
# repro harness (very small)
import requests, time, threading

def worker(token):
    for _ in range(20):
        r = requests.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}, json={"model":"redwood-large","input":"x","stream":True}, stream=True, timeout=3)
        try:
            for chunk in r.iter_content(chunk_size=None):
                pass
        except Exception as e:
            print("err", e)
        time.sleep(0.1)

# spawn concurrent workers simulating token churn
threads = []
for i in range(30):
    t = threading.Thread(target=worker, args=("token_rotating_%d"%i,))
    t.start()
    threads.append(t)
for t in threads: t.join()
```

This reproduces connection storm locally.

lex: Immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) throttle auth token rotation frequency on customer side (increase to >5m) 2) enable client-side connection reuse (keep-alive + HTTP/2 multiplexing) 3) short-term edge config: bump per-worker fd and queue thresholds, and enable a quick fallback to smaller model variant for that route so backend time per request drops.

emily: Runtime mitigation: enable a temporary lower batch expansion threshold and increase max concurrency for the redwood-large pool to reduce p95. Also toggle KV cache warmup to prepopulate common prefixes if possible. We can roll this change as a quick patch to dedicated pools for hosted customers.

marta: Draft customer message I plan to send after we apply mitigations: 

"Hi — thanks for the report and repro. We identified an interaction between frequent token rotation in your client and connection re-creation at the edge, which caused an ingress connection storm and elevated 502/504s. We're applying temporary mitigations now (edge queue thresholds and a lighter model fallback) and recommend increasing token TTL and enabling HTTP/2 connection reuse in your SDK. We'll follow up once we've validated the change. Apologies for the disruption." 

juan: Can we also check SDK v0.9.1 for a bug where it forcibly closes connections on token refresh? If so, we need a hotfix.

lex: Logged a quick trace: yes v0.9.1 has a path that closes the session in auth refresh routine instead of reusing. I will open a PR to ensure session.keepalive persists across refresh. That should reduce new connection rate massively.

ops-bot: deployment: edge-router config bump rolled to canary (2/10 hosts) at 13:14 UTC; runtime batch expansion tweak deployed to canary model pool at 13:16 UTC. Monitoring: queue depth down 70% on canary.

emily: Observability shows p95 generation latency across canary hosts dropped back below 500ms and 502s on canary are gone. We'll continue rollout if stable.

marta: Sending update to customer now with the draft above and note that we're continuing a full rollout.

juan: Follow-ups: create SDK ticket for v0.9.1 hotfix, add a guardrail in edge to rate-limit new connections per client-id, and codify recommended token TTL in docs.

marta: Created ticket and updated customer. Closing thread once full rollout completes and we confirm no recurrence.

lex: Adding postmortem stub: suspected causal chain = token rotation -> connection churn -> router fd/queue exhaustion -> 502/504 -> client retry fanout -> amplification. Remediation: SDK fix, edge rate-limits, docs, runtime defensive defaults.

marta: Thanks all :thumbsup:
